title: Crossing
style: cinematic horror film still, old car ferry crossing a black harbor at night, thick drifting sea fog, sodium deck lights, wet steel, rope and rust, cold teal and amber tones, dramatic moody lighting, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Final part. Owen rides the last ferry to the end. Now he knows where the missing go. 🌊

Original fiction. New series tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: twenty-three boarded Owen's ferry, twenty-two got off, and the captain said tonight the dead were counting.
scenes.image: footprints ending at a ferry rail above black water

scenes.narration: Owen won't leave. Someone is missing out there. So when Marta turns the ferry back into the fog, he stays aboard.
scenes.image: ferry pulling away from a foggy dock at night, a lone deckhand at the stern rail

scenes.narration: The water goes perfectly still. The engine stops. And the ferry keeps moving.
scenes.image: ferry gliding over glass-smooth black water in fog with no wake behind it

scenes.narration: Out of the fog comes another ship. Smaller. Older. Lit with yellow lamps. The Calloway. Dry. Whole. Like it never went down.
scenes.image: small old wooden ferry emerging from fog, glowing yellow lamps, perfectly intact, on still black water

scenes.narration: Its deck is crowded. Not with faces from the museum wall. With modern faces. Commuters. Nurses. Tonight's missing passenger. Years of missing passengers.
scenes.image: crowd of quiet modern people in coats standing at the rail of an old wooden ferry, faces pale in yellow lamplight

scenes.narration: And all around Owen, on his own benches, the passengers from 1961 sit quietly. Dripping. Smiling. Almost home.
scenes.image: ferry benches filled with quiet people in early nineteen-sixties coats and hats, soaked, smiling softly

scenes.narration: Owen finally understands. The extras weren't escaping. They were coming home. And every one who came home left an empty seat. Someone from this side had to fill it. Seat for seat.
scenes.image: two ferries side by side in fog, a narrow gap of black water between their rails

scenes.narration: At the Calloway's rail stands a man in an old deckhand's cap. Owen's grandfather. He looks at the last empty seat. Then at Owen.
scenes.image: young man in a vintage deckhand's cap at the rail of an old ferry, looking across the gap with sad eyes

scenes.narration: He steps across, dry for the first time in sixty-six years, and squeezes Owen's shoulder. Every crossing needs a deckhand, he says. Your turn to count.
scenes.image: old ferry pulling away into fog with a young deckhand in an orange jacket standing at its rail, looking back

scenes.narration: In the morning, the log reads twenty-four passengers, in Owen's handwriting. Nobody can find Owen. Tomorrow night: a dead man's radio that reads tomorrow's news.
scenes.image: vintage shortwave radio glowing warm on a wooden table in a dark room, dial lit amber
